newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Boatpeople to be stranded in Hong Kong after handover.
newsitem.headline: Boatpeople to be stranded in Hong Kong after handover.

text.p: Thousands of Vietnamese boatpeople will be stranded in Hong Kong after the handover to China on July 1, a local radio station reported on Wednesday.
This is despite Beijing's demands that the British-led administration in Hong Kong clear the remaining boatpeople in detention camps before China resumes sovereignty.
Peter Lai, Secretary for Security, was quoted by Radio Television Hong Kong as saying that at least 3,400 boatpeople will be left after the handover.
They include some 1,400 refugees, 900 others whose bid for asylum in third countries was rejected and 1,100 recent arrivals, the radio said.
However, an official with the United Nations refugee agency in Hong Kong said third countries have recently become more understanding, a local television station reported.

"We've asked resettlement countries to please be flexible and we've been encouraged by the response ...they've told us 'Okay send us these cases and we'll look at them'," said Paul Meredith of the United Nations High Commissioner for Refugees.
Lai and other government officials were not immediately available for comment on the reports.
